To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transjugular liver biopsies are safe and can be performed with high success and low complication rates.

transjugular liver biopsies are feasible in patients undergoing TIPS, with a low risk of complications, and are useful in identifying liver disease severity in these patients, and that transjugular biopsies are associated with a lower risk of bleeding than transcutaneous biopsies.

the use of TIPS for the treatment of refractory ascites is associated with an increase in the risk of mortality and that TIPS placement in the setting of a transjugular liver biopsies may not be associated with an increase risk of mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of transjugular biopsy and TIPS in the evaluation of portal hypertension.
the role of the liver in the development of hypertension.
the role of transjugular biopsy and TIPS for the evaluation of liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TIPS is a valuable procedure in patients with portal hypertension, but it should be performed by an experienced interventional radiologist in a tertiary care center.

TIPS should be performed in all patients with portal hypertension with a liver biopsy that shows a histological diagnosis that is consistent with the clinical diagnosis, and in all patients with a liver biopsy showing a diagnosis that is not consistent with the clinical findings.

the transjugular liver approach is not the first choice of liver biopsy, and it is not recommended in the presence of a normal liver function test, but it can be considered as a second choice in patients with coagulopathy and in patients with liver failure and ascites, as a safe procedure with minimal complications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transjugular liver biopsies (TJLB) are useful in the evaluation of patients with portal hypertension (PH) and liver cirrhosis (LC) and in the follow-up of patients with TIPS.
we are not able to predict the outcome of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic stent shunt (TIPS) in patients with liver cirrhosis and refractory ascites based on transjugular liver biopsies.
we have shown that the combination of transjugular biopsy and TIPS is a useful tool in the evaluation of the patient with portal hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of TIPS is higher in patients with a high MELD score and that this risk is further increased by the presence of severe fibrosis.
TIPS should be used with caution in patients with cirrhosis with portal hypertension.
TIPS is a safe procedure with low morbidity and mortality.
